trust_decision.summary: Whether a request address (a string from X-Forwarded-For or the socket peer) falls inside a configured trust subnet is decided at runtime by the compiled predicate trustSingle/trustMulti, which converts an IPv4 candidate to its IPv4-mapped IPv6 form (and an IPv6 candidate to IPv4) before delegating to ipaddr.js match() on the (subnet IP, prefix length) tuple produced at compile time.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary and its reproducer use one IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnet with a short prefix (e.g. '::ffff:10.0.0.0/8'); a one-element trust spec compiles to trustSingle at index.js:145, so an engineer who reads only the summary lands on the kind-mismatch conversion in trustSingle.

fix_sites.entry_point: proxyaddr.compile(trust) and proxyaddr(req, trust) / proxyaddr.all(req, trust) -> compiled predicate (canonicalize an IPv4-mapped candidate to IPv4)
fix_sites.module_kind: public API (library export) reaching an internal compiled predicate

fix_sites.entry_point: proxyaddr.compile([subnetA, subnetB, ...]) -> trustMulti cross-family conversion branch
proxyaddr.compile([...]) -> trustMulti same-family branch for a native IPv6 candidate against an IPv4-mapped subnet
proxyaddr.compile(trust) and proxyaddr(req, trust) / proxyaddr.all(req, trust) -> trustSingle (canonicalize an IPv4-mapped candidate to IPv4)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: index.js:254-291 (trustMulti, the multi-subnet implementation of the same predicate)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory's example is one subnet string, which compiles to trustSingle (index.js:144-145); trustMulti is a separate loop with its own one-shot ipconv cache, so a solver who reproduced the one-element/string case can argue that path is already fixed and the array path is out of the example's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnets with a prefix of at least /96 must keep matching IPv4 candidates ('::ffff:a00:2/122' must trust 10.0.0.1), IPv4 trust must keep matching an IPv4-mapped socket peer (::ffff:a00:1 trusts 10.0.0.1), and bare mapped host notation must keep being canonicalized at index.js:168-171. An over-broad fix (reject any IPv6 subnet for an IPv4 candidate, or drop all mapped subnets) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: IPv4 candidate ('8.8.8.8', '0.0.0.0', '120.0.0.1') against an IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnet - fix.diff:27-31
native IPv6 candidate ('::1', '::abcd', '::fffe:0:0') against a mapped subnet - fix.diff:40-42
single-subnet trust spec: a plain string or a one-element array, compiled to trustSingle - index.js:144-145
multi-subnet array, compiled to trustMulti (e.g. ['::ffff:10.0.0.0/8', '10.0.0.0/8']) - index.js:146
mapped subnet prefix lengths below 96, exactly 96 and above (/95, /96, /97, /104, /122) - fix.diff:27, fix.diff:64
plain IPv6 subnet ranging over IPv4 space ('::/1', 'fc00::/7', '2001:db8::/32') - fix.diff:128-139
named pre-defined ranges ('uniquelocal') spliced into the subnet list - index.js:102-109

O7_producer.where: index.js:156-196 (parseipNotation builds the [ip, prefixLength] subnet tuple at compile time)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a named pre-defined range containing an IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnet (e.g. 'mappeduniquelocal': ['::ffff:10.0.0.0/104'])
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: maintainers already keep a table of shorthand names here and it is spliced straight into the same trust list at index.js:102-109, so a new name would silently reach the same sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: accepting netmask notation on an IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnet ('::ffff:10.0.0.0/255.0.0.0'), a second notation route producing a mapped subnet tuple
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the parser already supports two notations for IPv4 and the netmask branch is gated only on kind() === 'ipv4', so relaxing it is a small, plausible generalisation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a family-specific fast path in compileTrust (e.g. a compiled IPv4-only predicate reused for a mapped IPv6 subnet)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: compileTrust already returns specialised implementations by subnet count, so an added 'same-family only' optimisation is in keeping with the file's style

O9_family: IP source-address spoofing / trust-boundary bypass (CWE-290 authentication bypass by spoofing, CWE-348, CWE-697)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; Node.js per engines >= 0.10 (CI matrix .github/workflows/ci.yml:17-44); mocha 8.4.0 + nyc for tests; eslint for lint; dependencies forwarded@0.2.0 and ipaddr.js@1.9.1 (package.json:17-20)
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.js run by `npm test` (mocha --reporter spec --bail --check-leaks, package.json:47), ~510 lines; relevant suites are 'when IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses' at test/test.js:278-320 and 'proxyaddr.compile(trust)' at test/test.js:442-500; no network or fixtures needed, tests use hand-built request objects (test/test.js:502-509)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject the cross-family conversion outright (or drop/refuse IPv4-mapped IPv6 subnets) once the short-prefix case is reproduced on trustSingle, which fixes '::ffff:10.0.0.0/8' but breaks the /122 mapped-subnet and mapped-socket-peer behaviour asserted at test/test.js:278-319.

unverified: repo_mb is null: no shell was available to measure the tree; the source is one 328-line index.js plus tests and four benchmark scripts, clearly far under 5 MB, hence tiny_repo.

j_defence_ineffective=1 is a judgement call: the 'Incompatible IP addresses' family guard at index.js:270-273 and index.js:314-317 is present and admits every IPv4-mapped candidate unconditionally, and index.js:168-171 canonicalizes mapped notation only when no prefix is given; this is counted as a defence present but ineffective, not as a documented mitigation.

Whether ipaddr.js@1.9.1 match() has any additional mapped-address special case was not inspected (dependency source is not in the pinned tree); all conclusions follow from the pinned index.js code flow.

O1=3 counts the three exported functions (proxyaddr index.js:222, proxyaddr.all index.js:55, proxyaddr.compile index.js:84) that reach the flaw; if entry points are counted per compiled predicate (trustSingle/trustMulti) the number is 2.
